requirements.text: Mara's evening work made visits difficult, while she still cared about sharing stories
Sol held back because he thought his ordinary, unfinished stories would not interest others
Grandma observed fewer visits and interpreted them as lost interest
The decline began before the storm damaged the crossing
Try a compact story adventure in a fixed-camera 3D world with direct character/object interaction, using the agreed story and literacy goals
Work through one concrete encounter together, then judge a playable version before committing the whole story to the approach
Judge the candidate by coherent scale/presentation, clear meaningful actions and feedback, useful reading, and lasting story consequences; current implementation/reuse is not the quality target
Connect the first mission to Mara's work conflict, Pip's planting promise, and taking Mara's actual story and explanation to Grandma; keep the setting coherent and the dialogue useful
Let the child guide Pip, briefly arrange the movable paper boats as director while Pip waits, connect the crossing, and then separately guide Pip across
Show an actual remaining gap and the accepted feedback when a placement falls short; allow immediate adjustment while retaining the seed and page

Preserve the constructed crossing, carry the actual seed/page, visibly plant with Grandma, and perform the actual page handoff and shown report/reply; the crossing alone does not resolve Mara's work conflict
Keep contextual meaning and pronunciation available in the encounter, including obligation in Mara's account, with return to the same passage and world; lookup use is assistance

Show a wider river stretch near arrival and a narrower stretch upstream; the same joined boats fall short at the wider location and reach both banks at the narrower one, with constant dimensions and visible reach
Let the child choose a location, move/join the boats in the scene, and visibly fasten one end of the crossing to each bank
Show the actual remaining gap or loose end with the exact accepted feedback; permit adjustment and first-attempt success without a required mistake
Present the exact construction instruction and contextual secure definition above; connect the existing meaning/pronunciation support to this encounter
Once the crossing is usable, let the child separately guide Pip across with his actual possessions; preserve the crossing for return trips and later story use
Let the child write a short ending using Sol's original account and disclosed later events; use the shown prompt and keep the source and child's wording available
Try my ending rehearses the player's chosen emphasis through the workbench paper scene: baking, later thanks, or both in order; Pip and Sol remain beside the scene
Preserve the draft for revision, give the exact demonstrated leak-versus-rain feedback for that example, and retain prepared endings and the original Draft to discuss route as valid alternatives
Retain the selected player wording and scene emphasis for Sol's actual contribution at the gathering; trying a version, choosing it, and later sharing remain distinct
Keep contextual word help and optional aloud practice of the chosen ending available; the detailed practice/audio interface remains open
Use AI to interpret freely written endings and give focused revision help within defined story characters, events, and actions; exact AI contracts and fallback remain open

Make the gathering time decision with Grandma, ask Mara about her later reading/listening role in person, notify Sol, and report actual arrangements; preserve the difference between a proposed plan and each completed conversation
Use the exact shown later/Mara time choice, Grandma response, Sol notice/reply, Mara invitation/reply, and return report/readiness response with their actual starting conditions
Retain the later/Mara, later/Pip-with-Mara-listening, and usual/Pip routes as valid choices with their actual participation and closing consequences

Begin the gathering triggers the short event transition appropriate to the plan: on the later route the boat returns, Mara finishes her passenger duty then walks across, and Sol arrives from his workshop with his prepared story

Retain Sol's actual selected ending and completed work through planning and notification; use postpone/postponed meaningfully in the shown explanation and invitation, with existing reading support available
Show Jo, the paper story, and Loop ready with the shown purpose line; use D022's introduction and make Begin Pip's adventure immediately available
Use the shown D018 river promise/letter, Start playing, and visible planting goal; keep the opening and letter recoverable
Introduce the shown arrow/WASD movement prompt, suggested Mara step, named nearby click/E conversation, and word-help hint with obligation; allow boats-first exploration
Retain the planting promise when the actual Mara page handoff adds the delivery task
At construction, provide Arrange boats, the shown director/Pip role explanation, and Back to Pip
Keep Help available for the current goal, opening/letter, and controls when the introduction is skipped or forgotten, without requiring a restart
Show the small current-goal card and one suggested next action; after Mara's real page handoff retain the exact planting goal and add the shown carrying reminder
Update the shown guidance after a usable crossing, actual planting, and actual Mara sharing; retain the visible crossing, rooted seed flower, and real lantern contribution
Where is that? briefly identifies the suggested known destination by name; the child still moves Pip and solves the challenge
Adapt to the shown Grandma-first visit without forcing the Mara-first suggestion or repeating completed planting
Help includes Story so far with brief actual-event statements and a useful next action; use the shown planted/held-page/unheard-story recap only when true
Use the shown Sol preparation/report goals; retain chosen wording or valid original draft, including work from an earlier visit

Get ready for the gathering selects an actually unfinished time/role/notice/report action; either outstanding visit can occur first; use the shown changed-time Plan/Sol reminder and remove it after the actual update
Keep guidance relevant during reading/writing/talking; preserve completed work and suggest useful nearby conversations before another journey

Once applicable preparations are complete, show Begin the gathering when you're ready; during actual gathering scenes use the shown welcome, first-story, Sol invitation, Grandma story, and Pip moment prompts
Show Finish Pip's adventure after the applicable closing; for absent Mara first require the actual Grandma-story delivery and allow finishing at the dock
In the resulting studio presentation show Show how Pip's adventure ended with the agreed Watch the ending and Narrate the ending options
Use Pip, Mara, Sol, Grandma, Jo, and Loop in the shown roles, preserving the distinction between the four story characters and the two studio figures
Use one studio scene and the connected riverbank/dock, Grandma garden, and Sol-workshop areas, with the shown activities; distinguish Sol's workshop from the former studio Workshop
Leave Remy, Ari, Maximum Toast, and separate studio Courtyard/Workshop/Media routes outside this demo's playable flow; preserve the Loop-ready entry and ending presentation

Use the shown roles/actions/results for the boats, broken bridge, passenger dock/boat, seed/planting place, letter/pages/manuscript, lanterns, scenery, and studio story/projector/display; retain their actual source and possession distinctions
Use posts/ropes to show the crossing's two bank attachments; Fasten this end visibly secures one end; retain the shown loose-end response and separate return to Pip control
Let the child open a simple backpack contents view reflecting actual possessions; remove items from that view when planted or handed over
Give usable world objects clear highlights and named actions when targeted; distinguish scenery and add no collection/furniture-arranging task to the shown bench/cushion/plant/tool roles
Make proportions explain use: carryable pages, backpack fitting Pip, a believable joined-boat walking surface, and furniture fitting the cast; moving boats preserves their size
Use short direct instructions, natural conversations with clear speakers available during response selection, and complete titled/attributed story pages with readable paragraphs
Use the exact complete The Torn Wing page above with Mara as author/narrator in the applicable actual story encounter
On requested hesitated help, show the exact demonstrated definition/context, offer word/sentence pronunciation, and return to the same page; retain help for other unfamiliar words
Connect the page to the shown equally valid promise/repair illustrations; change the picture on the same contribution and keep the page reopenable from its lantern
Present the exact original A Small Repair manuscript with Sol's authorship and Ending not written yet outside the fresh manuscript; retain any actually selected version on revisit
After the actual offer to help, keep Sol's exact additional account under What Sol tells you next, distinct from and available with the original manuscript during writing
Use Your ending for Sol's story, the exact prompt and perspective reminder; start the new writing box empty and retain the child's draft when support is used

Retain word help, comparison with the source, Try my ending rehearsal of supported consequences, revision, prepared support and the original-draft alternative without requiring independent writing to continue
Supply Sol's reason through the exact shown exchange with Grandma before she reads the complete attributed The Empty Bench page; preserve actual prior knowledge and contribution/attendance facts
Retain optional narration and word help, including the shown assumed definition/context and word/sentence/return support
Offer the optional storm question with the exact reply and relevant chronology sentences highlighted; ordinary continuation stays available
Record the actual Grandma contribution in its existing rooted lantern with the cushions illustration, keep the same page reopenable, and continue the actual Pip-moment and Mara closing route
Begin the garden with exactly these two complete older story pages under the shown titles/authors, retaining their availability alongside new contributions and after the chapter
Use the shown picnic and flute/whistling illustration subjects to identify historical accounts; preserve their authorship and distinct older-story identity
Let the child approach a pictured lantern, open Read story, use optional help, close the page and resume the current activity; reading either older page remains optional

Show the exact secure definition/context above with word/sentence pronunciation and return; retain unfamiliar-word support, including hesitated and duet, with their complete context-specific coverage still to be defined
Assemble the ending in the shown four-paragraph order from the exact common planting, actual Mara, actual Sol and applicable closing paragraphs
Match pictures to actual attendance/storyteller, Sol contribution, absent-Mara delivery and selected Pip lantern moment
Retain Jo's exact presentation invitation and Watch the ending / Narrate the ending, with the same outcome text and child-paced advancement in Narrate
Preserve Sol's exact selected story wording or original draft and actual completed events when preparing or playing their summary
Retain the exact shown later/Mara-listening choice, Grandma reply, actual invitation/acceptance, truthful report and complete welcome
Retain the exact shown usual/Pip choice, Grandma response, Sol time notice/report and complete welcome, using already supplied Mara permission
Keep actual notices, readiness, arrivals, storyteller/listener roles, Sol's selected contribution and applicable closing consistent with the spoken words
Offer Practise a part from the actual Mara page with the exact boy's excerpt and Read the boy's words aloud. Pause briefly at each full stop.
Hear this part provides the exact spoken model; My turn stops that model and retains the words while the child reads at their own pace, with meaning/pronunciation support
Try the last sentence shows the exact final sentence with promised emphasized and the exact explanatory cue, optional model and rereading
Back to the story returns to the same page/activity; practice is optional and supplies reading support without claiming to have heard or assessed the child
Offer optional Read with feedback with visible listening and Stop, retaining D044's independent practice without a microphone
Give at most one supported source-word suggestion at a time; retain the exact brother/sister example, source highlight and replay/model/retry/continue choices
Allow the shown I said sister disagreement and exact reply; retain unclear-audio response without marking an uncertain word wrong or requiring agreement/retry
Keep current feedback focused on word-reading accuracy; full pronunciation/prosody/fluency judgments require separate scope and qualification
Record AI/language-learning expansion as a future possibility only; current scope and implementation mechanism remain bounded as stated above
Use the exact word-match response only for a supported match; offer replay, expression practice or return without claiming perfect pronunciation or fluency
Use the exact retry and self-correction responses only when new audio supports them; do not demand another attempt after self-correction
Use the exact microphone-unavailable and feedback-unavailable messages, preserving available independent practice
Use the exact example-voice unavailable message and retain visible words and reading tips
Keep the passage and story progress; allow return to the adventure from every shown outcome
Read my ending aloud opens the actual current ending beside the distinct Try my ending scene preview; the sample is not a prefilled answer
Show the exact initial pause instruction; Hear this part models the same words, My turn is independent, and Read with feedback remains an explicit option with D045-D046 behavior
Read it again uses the exact meaning/emphasis cue; the sample phrase is one possible choice, not required or scored
Allow contextual meaning/pronunciation help and the shown Listen to the word, then try it in the sentence cue when audio is available
Back to my ending retains wording and writing/story options; practice stays optional, supplied-ending practice is valid, and the original unfinished draft remains a valid route
Offer Narrate with feedback directly at the ending; listen during an explicitly selected reading and respond after each short paragraph, retaining optional support
Use the exact supported problem/promise feedback, word model and sentence retry; allow disputed recognition and uncertainty without forced agreement
Support how words are spoken using actual audio, model and retry; distinguish a recognized-word match from pronunciation evidence
Ask the exact kept-his-promise meaning question, accept an equivalent own-words explanation and use the shown follow-up for He crossed the river; keep this evidence separate from reading accuracy
After the existing later-gathering offer, ask the exact How would starting later help me get to the gathering question; allow an own-words spoken or typed explanation and the shown supported reply
For the demonstrated bridge-only explanation, use the exact crossing-versus-work-time follow-up; keep the actual passage, help and continuation available
Retain the actual next planning conversations and eventual boat/passenger/arrival consequences; a spoken or typed explanation alone cannot perform them
Preserve the other valid sharing plans, equivalent explanations and optional support; choosing a workable option or copying help alone is not independent comprehension evidence
Retain the existing offer, permission and page handoff; then ask the exact How could I get one of Grandma's stories if I'm still at work question and accept an equivalent own-words explanation

Use Please ask Grandma if she'd like to send me one for the shown copy proposal; for I'll read your story at the garden use the exact That lets Grandma hear my story follow-up; retain source/help/continuation
Keep the actual Grandma agreement, gathering, copy creation and delivery as separate actions; preserve the other valid plans and distinguish assistance/choice/delivery from independent understanding
Keep the encountered Grandma/Mara passages available and ask the exact reason question before Pip supplies the answer; retain the actual page handoff
Accept an equivalent own-words explanation, then use the exact short Pip page/request line and existing Grandma response
For the shown repeated assumption, offer the exact I miss it source hint; Let Pip explain uses the original factual report and continues
Distinguish independent explanation, help and supplied report; retain actual source/report and story continuity rather than inferring understanding from a control selection
Keep the unchanged Mara page available and ask the exact motive question before supplying an interpretation
Respond to the shown explanation as possible, accepting other text-supported interpretations without requiring a phrase or asserting an unstated thought as fact
For the shown claim that Mara tore the wing when reaching, give the exact sequence-based help, retain the page and allow revision, help or continuation
Preserve both equal lantern pictures and the existing default; distinguish inference from source fact and supplied help from independent explanation
With the actual original and later sources available, rehearse the brief thanks ending using the existing visit scene and retain it as a valid choice
Offer the exact repair-consequence prompt as optional development help; retain the child's words, source access and alternatives
Rehearse the shown supported revision using repair/dry flour, baking and later thanks in order, with the exact response connecting repair to Rina's promise
Keep thanks, baking and combined emphases valid; separate prompted revision, supplied help, rehearsal, selection and actual sharing
Retain the hesitated definition and bird-context help; use the exact flute-context explanation for that occurrence without asserting an unspoken motive
Offer the word and actual selected sentence as audio and return to the same page/reading position
Preserve help beyond selected teaching words and on revisits; retain optional story encounters and distinguish supplied help from independent word understanding
After the actual crossing interaction and optional picnic-page encounter, offer the exact secure question, accept an equivalent explanation and give the exact stones/fastenings comparison
For the shown stopping-the-wind explanation, give the exact still-blowing-wind hint; retain the passage, word support, retry and continuation
Preserve the existing crossing and optional story, actual encounter conditions and bounded evidence; add no new physical task, required mistake, word-mastery badge or answer gate
Use secure, obligation, postpone/postponed, hesitated, mended and assumed as the demo's six focus words with the shown meanings; mended means Repaired something that was damaged
Connect the words to their actual story/actions and distinguish a repeated word from reuse of its meaning; preserve conditional encounters and optional routes
Keep help for other unfamiliar words/phrases and accept clear own-words explanations without requiring the target term or a completed vocabulary list
Clicking kept in the actual ending highlights kept his promise and shows the exact phrase definition and planting-context explanation
Clicking put in the picnic sentence highlights stayed put and shows the exact phrase definition and cloth/stones explanation
Offer pronunciation of the selected word, relevant phrase and actual sentence, returning to the same page/paragraph and position
Preserve optional/repeatable help, the six-word focus, story progress and separate meaning-question evidence; help is assistance, not independent mastery
Show the exact mended, postponed and prevented definitions/context explanations for their actual applicable occurrences
Offer the exact duet definition from the title; add the exact performers explanation only after that passage is reached
Offer the actual word and sentence, or Hear the title for The Unexpected Duet, then return to the same reading position
Preserve source and route conditions, help beyond the focus set and optional reading; lookup/playback does not advance the story or establish learning
Ground feedback in the original story, actually supplied later facts and the child's current ending
Adapt feedback to acknowledge a clear supported connection, correct the specific misunderstanding or offer targeted development, as illustrated above
Respond to the revised meaning and stop repeating a resolved correction; recognize supported paraphrases without required keywords
Keep draft feedback distinct from existing-scene selection and from unagreed learning-history personalization; preserve equal emphases and optional support
Treat the demonstrated ending as supported but insufficient to identify a scene; ask the shown clarification instead of calling it a factual error or guessing a rehearsal
Retain the draft in the existing writing interaction; after the demonstrated revision and another Try my ending, rehearse the later visit with the child's exact words and relevant feedback
Keep actual sources and existing prepared-ending support available; preserve optional revision and valid alternative contributions

Use an existing language model with actual story facts, instructions and the draft to assess described event, factual fit and sufficient scene information; interpret varied wording rather than enumerating phrases
Keep unclear-for-scene-selection distinct from clear-but-contradictory writing; let the game handle the permitted response, with structural validity distinct from semantic correctness
Evaluate varied drafts beyond the supplied examples and provide a way to correct model interpretation; exact evaluation and correction interaction remain to specify
Offer That's not what I meant beside the rehearsal; selecting it stops the mistaken scene, retains the draft and shows the agreed clarification response
Offer the three named clickable illustrated previews for the existing disclosed baking, thanks and combined scenes
Selecting Rina brings Sol a loaf directly rehearses the later visit with unchanged writing and Showing Rina's visit; no further AI interpretation or rewrite is required
Keep correcting a rehearsal separate from final ending selection and actual story sharing; normal play need not include a model error
Offer Check that feedback; retain the exact draft, withdraw the disputed advice as current and open the actual source, including the shown excerpt for this case
Recheck the disputed criticism once against the original page, disclosed later account and current draft; replace the demonstrated false claim with the appropriate source-supported correction
If unresolved, use the shown response and retain writing, sources and existing support without reinstating the disputed advice or automatically declaring the child correct
If AI writing feedback is unavailable after Try my ending, preserve the exact draft and show the agreed notice
Offer Choose a scene with D061's three illustrated choices; selecting the thanks scene directly rehearses the visit with unchanged writing and the existing confirmation
Keep the original and later accounts, Show an example for existing supplied endings, continued writing and the original draft-discussion route available
Keep feedback unavailability clear and distinguish the child's scene choice from AI assessment; preserve play through existing authored routes
Show Looking at your ending... after Try my ending while keeping the editor usable
On the shown edit, retain the new draft and show the exact changed-ending notice; ignore the earlier response and require an explicit new Try my ending to request feedback for the revision
Offer Stop feedback while waiting; retain writing, show the exact stopped response and allow continued writing or direct scene choice
Prevent an obsolete or stopped reply from displaying old advice, modifying writing or taking over the selected rehearsal; editing alone submits no request
Use an existing complete prepared contextual card when it matches the word's actual use

Otherwise preserve a matching reviewed basic meaning and ask AI for context; if no suitable reviewed meaning exists, AI may supply both meaning and context using the actual selected word/sentence/surrounding text
The dragged example establishes the demonstrated meaning and contextual response quality; examples are authored illustrations, not actual model results or mandatory verbatim generated output
Retain Hear the word and Hear the sentence for the actual source targets and return to the same reading position without changing the story
Prepare and review locally stored basic meanings for every selectable word use in the demo's fixed reading material, matching each actual context
When additional AI word help is unavailable, use the stored meaning and the shown unavailable-context notice; retain actual source, listening controls and reading position
Preserve complete authored cards and matching reviewed meanings during normal AI context help as well as fallback; distinguish fixed-text coverage from arbitrary new child-written words
Use Read my ending aloud and the child's actual current word/sentence for help, as in the appreciation example
Offer the illustrated contextual meaning and sentence explanation; distinguish word help from checking the whole ending's factual fit
Retain actual word/sentence listening, return to the same paragraph and leave writing unchanged; reuse a stored meaning only when it fits the current use
If neither AI help nor an appropriate stored meaning is available, show the exact unavailable-help response and retain paragraph, available pronunciation and writing/return actions
Keep a matching reviewed definition fixed during normal word help; AI may add context, with complete prepared cards still preferred
Offer Check this explanation; withdraw the disputed generated explanation while retaining the actual sentence/meaning and request one recheck against those references

Replace the shown carrying error with an appropriate source-supported explanation; if unresolved, retain the reviewed meaning with D066's notice or use D067's notice when no suitable meaning exists for child-written text
Retain source/writing/listening/return and require evaluation of generated explanations; a dispute or recheck alone establishes neither correctness nor learning
On requested help for the shown apreciation occurrence, use the actual spelling/sentence to offer the appreciation suggestion and shown meaning
Offer Hear suggested word for the displayed candidate, clearly distinguished from the unchanged original spelling
Use appreciation replaces only the selected occurrence and retains all other wording; Keep what I wrote preserves the original and returns to reading
Show the suggestion on a word-help request and change writing only after the child's explicit choice; retain subsequent reading and normal story access
Use the actual current question, relevant disclosed Mara account and current child answer to adapt feedback through Mara
Recognize the supported work-time connection and equivalent wording, retaining the shown acknowledgement and actual next planning action
Use the shown clarifying follow-up for more time without labeling it wrong; address the boat-speed misunderstanding with the shown source-based correction
Retain rereading, help and continuation; feedback alone does not arrange the gathering or change work, travel or attendance
Offer Check that feedback for the shown conversation misreading; retain the exact child answer, withdraw the disputed reply and open Mara's actual explanation
Recheck once using the actual question, source, current answer and disputed reply; give an appropriate correction for the shown misreading without rewriting the answer or performing the plan
If unresolved, show the separate interface notice and retain the answer, sources and planning access without mandatory rewriting, repeated argument or automatic correctness
When conversation feedback is unavailable, retain the exact answer and show the separate Feedback isn't available right now notice without inventing an assessment
Offer Reread Mara's explanation, Help me explain and Continue planning with the shown source/answer continuity and actual next planning step
Show the exact prepared explanation under Help, available without AI and separate from the unchanged child answer; support remains available when AI is working
Allow the child to revise or continue; supplied help is assistance, and continuation still requires the real Grandma conversation rather than automatically arranging the gathering
Compare the actual recording with its displayed passage using sound-based assessment; a matching transcript alone does not establish pronunciation accuracy
Select one reviewed practice prompt from a supported finding; highlight hesitated and show the exact prompt for the demonstrated case
Provide Hear my reading, Hear hesitated, Hear the sentence, Try the sentence and Back to the story with their actual recording, word, sentence and return targets
Base retry feedback on the new recording, retain the shown uncertainty response and optional continuation, and do not infer improvement merely from retrying
For a recording-supported sentence-boundary difficulty after come, highlight that actual full stop and show the exact short-pause prompt
Offer Hear my reading, Hear this part, Read it again and Back to the story with actual/model audio, unchanged excerpt and the same story return
Retain Try the last sentence and the promised emphasis cue as a meaningful practice choice, without grading emotion or requiring an identical performance
Give one suggestion at a time; do not require a fixed pause length, compulsory reread or treat every difference from the model as an error
Opening Read with feedback leaves the microphone off and shows both pre-recording notices; only explicit Start listening with applicable permission begins capture
Show actual Listening/Stop state; Stop ends capture and shows the review notice without sending audio; keep capture off during playback and feedback
Hear my reading replays the local attempt, Get feedback explicitly sends that recording and its passage reference, and Discard recording removes the unsent attempt; replay is optional
Back to the story stops capture, discards unsent audio and preserves reading position/progress; retry returns to readiness and requires another explicit start
Retain only the current recording for replay during practice after feedback and show the exact recording-lifetime explanation
Remove the local attempt when leaving practice or starting a new recording; reopening practice has no previous recording or feedback
Exclude recordings from game saves, recording files and routine logs, while preserving normal story-progress and written-ending save behavior
After explicit Get feedback, show Checking your reading with the microphone off, retain replay/model/return and prevent duplicate active submissions
Stop feedback shows the recording-retained notice, keeps practice available and ignores replies from the stopped request; a new check requires an explicit request
Leaving practice or starting a new recording invalidates old feedback; a late response cannot reopen practice, restore removed recordings or attach to a new attempt
A failed or timed-out request ends waiting with D046's exact unavailable-feedback notice, retains the current practice recording and does not retry automatically
Deliver reliable AI feedback quickly enough for the bounded demo while preserving the agreed task behavior and correction/failure routes; judge actual usable responses, not model branding

Leave routine model/service choice to implementation within the agreed requirements; record and qualify the eventual selection without asking Tony to approve a brand or requiring an exhaustive vendor comparison
Offer Give me a hint for the shown Mara question and display the exact prepared hint locally, leaving the child's answer unchanged
Keep rereading, full explanation and continuation directly available without a prior hint, mistake or waiting period; help does not complete the actual plan or establish independent comprehension
Resolve routine details using existing answers and record their source; stop requesting serial approval for each model, label or repeated support pattern
Ask only about material choices not inferable from prior answers, with a concrete consequence and recommendation; prioritize the bounded demo under the reported time constraint
Target children ages 9-12 and write the game for that audience
Include challenging words within the age range and some somewhat beyond it
Provide word help activated by clicking a word when the child needs it
Explain the selected word's meaning in relation to the passage being read
Provide help that lets the child learn how to pronounce the selected word
Treat fluency, comprehension, and vocabulary improvement as the intended educational purpose
The current player journey must not require a parent/teacher facilitator
The game must supply the guidance and reading help needed to understand its purpose, operate it, make progress, and recover from confusion
Connect reading, decisions, visible consequences, revisiting language, and narration within the same story
Let information in the text inform meaningful choices and show consequences; provide opportunities to explain or reconsider using the text
Provide short oral-reading practice, optional modeling and phrase support, and purposeful rereading for narration
Extend D002's contextual meaning/pronunciation help with meaningful later encounters or use of selected words
Develop bounded AI collaboration using supported story possibilities and the child's contributions
Expand beyond the small variations of the current seed/crossing sequence
Require more thought while retaining D007's literacy purpose
Define a finite collection of characters, props, actions, and consequences
Present the lantern garden as a living library whose flowers display illustrated moments from shared stories
Make why the garden fell quiet the central mystery
Connect that premise to D007/D009's director/narrator role and meaningful choices
Explain each interaction with natural, clear language and the exact passage, player actions, game responses, and next step
Mara's passage distinguishes her continued interest, earlier work-hours change, and later storm; keep the passage available while the player chooses what Pip says

The player can offer to ask Grandma for a later gathering or offer to read Mara's story; the first creates a request to discuss and the second gives Pip the page and permission to share it, with the stated next objectives
The bridge-only proposal gets Mara's explanation and the relevant work-hours sentences; the child may reread, make another offer, or leave and return
The demonstrated obligation card explains the word's meaning in Mara's situation and offers word/sentence pronunciation and return to the passage
The illustrated story-delivery path offers the exact closing narration, a spoken model, visible pauses, rereading, and Continue; oral practice is optional and does not claim assessed speech
Let the child choose which supported moment from Mara's shared story is displayed in its lantern-flower
The boy holding the torn bird and Mara/the boy repairing it are both valid; the chosen illustration and caption reflect that moment without changing the underlying events
Keep the full story available to reopen, and allow the displayed moment to be changed without duplicating the contribution or imposing a correct-answer score
Sol states his concern about the ordinary, unfinished story and offers the exact A Small Repair passage for the child to read
Offer either finishing the ending together or sharing the draft and asking listeners what they want to hear more about; both are valid contributions
In the completion path, Sol supplies the additional bakery/thank-you events; either shown ending can be selected and previewed, preserving those facts and his authorship
